name: China economy
summary: China's property investment fell 21.6% in the first ten months and new home prices fell again in October; slump persists
state: China's statistics bureau reported on 16 Nov that real estate development investment fell 21.6% year on year in January–October (NBS), while October retail sales rose only 0.4% and CPI 0.7% (China Briefing, 19 Nov). New home prices fell 0.1% month on month in October and 2.4% year on year, the slowest annual decline since November 2025 (The Standard, 16 Nov). GDP grew 4.6% in the first three quarters, within the 4.5–5% target. The property slump keeps Watch; no hard landing below 3% growth, financial contagion or sharp capital-control tightening was found as of 28 Nov.
for_you: Exporters, commodity producers and firms selling into China are most exposed to weak Chinese household demand. A prolonged property slump tends to weigh on construction materials prices and on local-government finances.
rubric_hit: Watch: prolonged property slump (real estate investment −21.6% y/y Jan–Oct); growth 4.6% vs < 3% Alert line

rubric.alert: Hard landing (growth < 3%), financial contagion, or capital controls tightened sharply.
rubric.watch: Deflation, renewed property-developer defaults, or growth clearly below target.
rubric.normal: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.
